title: The Needs Stack: positioning against competitors by climbing your customer's chain of goals
summary: Jason Cohen explains the Needs Stack: every customer need is a means to a higher need, and a product serving a higher level makes lower-level products obsolete. He shows how to use it for positioning (features at the customer's current level, benefits one level up), for competitive attack, for choosing metrics, and for finding higher purpose.

principles.text: Map your customer's Needs Stack: each need is a means to a higher need. Customers rarely want what you literally sell.
principles.quote: You need to understand the Needs Stack of your target customers. Not just your "market" or your "product" or "solving the problem" or even the immediate Jobs-To-Be-Done of your customer--those are all means to ends.

principles.text: Your real competitors include anyone serving a higher level of the stack, because they make your level obsolete.
principles.quote: a company who provides the higher-level need of "WordPress site" makes the lower-level need of "infrastructure" *obsolete*.

principles.text: Higher-level products trade flexibility for speed to the goal. Lower-level products keep customization. Both survive for different customers.
principles.quote: Up the stack, customers achieve their end-goal faster; down the stack, customers have more flexibility and customization.

principles.text: Resolve 'sell benefits vs features': talk features at the level the customer is thinking, and sell the benefit one level higher.
principles.quote: If someone has in their head "get a WordPress site," you want to meet them where they are, and talk about how your product is the best way to "get a WordPress site." That's the part where you talk about features.

principles.text: Position lower levels as irrelevant by focusing on the next level up, so the customer sees your product as the end, not a means.
principles.quote: In short, make "infrastructure" irrelevant by focusing on the next level up. The customer never wanted to think about infrastructure in the first place.

principles.text: Measure one level above your product to predict long-run retention, even if you can't control it. Shopify reports GMV for this reason.
principles.quote: It's strategic to measure further up the stack. Not too far, otherwise it's not only difficult to measure, but too many external factors drive the number. But the very next level up could be a critical way to measure value
